newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing pay awards unmoved in Q4 - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing pay awards unmoved in Q4 - CBI.

text.p: Manufacturing pay awards in Britain showed no signs of picking up in the last quarter of 1996, the Confederation of British Industry said on Monday.

The CBI's pay databank showed pay rises averaged a provisional 3.1 percent over the three months ending in December, unchanged from the third quarter and well down on the 3.7 percent average seen in the last three months of 1995.

One third of manufacturing firms surveyed said an inability to raise prices was keeping the lid on wage increases. Just under a quarter cited low profits as the main restraint while 20 percent said the low rise in the cost of living justified modest pay rises.

Underlying inflation, excluding mortgage interest payments, was running at an annual 3.1 percent in January, unchanged from December and exactly the same as the average pay rise, as measured by the CBI.
In the service sector, pay awards averaged 3.8 percent in the three months ending in December, compared with 3.6 percent in the previous quarter and 3.4 percent in the same period in 1995.
